metadata.name: IRS CP14 Balance Due Notice Response
metadata.description: Respond to IRS CP14, the first notice and demand for payment of an unpaid balance. Covers payment, installment agreements, offers in compromise, hardship status, penalty relief, and disputing an incorrect assessment.
metadata.searchVolumeSource: Google Ads Keyword Planner — 'CP14 notice', 'IRS notice CP14', 'CP14 payment'

verified.note: CP14 is the highest-volume IRS notice. Confirmed as notice and demand under IRC 6303; the pay-by date is printed on the notice rather than fixed by statute.

extraction.description: Extract the balance breakdown from a CP14. Unlike an underreporter notice there are no proposed line-item adjustments — the tax is already assessed. What matters is the composition of the balance: tax versus penalties versus interest, because each is contested and relieved differently.

fields.name: taxpayerName
fields.prompt: Extract the full taxpayer name from the notice header, exactly as printed.
fields.notes: For a joint return both names appear; capture the primary filer first.

fields.name: ssn
fields.prompt: Extract the Social Security Number or ITIN. Format as XXX-XX-XXXX. CP14 often shows only the last four digits — if so, return what is shown.
fields.notes: If truncated on the notice, the full number must come from the taxpayer, not be inferred.

fields.name: taxYear
fields.prompt: Extract the tax period the balance relates to. Look for 'Tax year' or 'Tax period' in the header. Return the 4-digit year.
fields.notes: A CP14 covers a single period. Multiple periods generate separate notices.

fields.name: noticeDate
fields.prompt: Extract the notice date from the top right of the notice. Format YYYY-MM-DD.
fields.notes: Interest and the failure-to-pay penalty are computed to this date.

fields.name: responseDeadline
fields.prompt: Extract the payment due date printed on the notice — usually phrased 'Pay by' or 'Amount due by'. Format YYYY-MM-DD. Do NOT compute this; CP14 prints its own date and that date controls.
fields.notes: Typically about 21 days out. Never substitute a calculated date for the printed one.

fields.name: taxOwed
fields.prompt: Extract the assessed TAX amount alone, excluding penalties and interest. Look for a line labelled 'Tax you owed' or similar in the balance breakdown.
fields.notes: Separating tax from penalty matters: penalties can be abated while the tax stands.

fields.name: penaltyAmount
fields.prompt: Extract the total penalties charged. Look for 'Failure-to-pay penalty', 'Failure-to-file penalty', or a combined 'Penalties' line.
fields.notes: Zero or absent is normal when the return was filed and only payment is late.

fields.name: penaltyTypes
fields.prompt: Extract which penalties were assessed, as a list of labels exactly as the notice names them. Common values: 'Failure to file', 'Failure to pay', 'Estimated tax penalty'.
fields.notes: Drives relief eligibility: First Time Abate covers failure-to-file and failure-to-pay, but not the estimated tax penalty.

fields.name: interestAmount
fields.prompt: Extract the interest charged. Look for a line labelled 'Interest charges'.
fields.notes: Interest on the tax is statutory and generally not abatable; interest on an abated penalty comes off with it.

fields.name: totalAmountDue
fields.prompt: Extract the total amount due — the large figure the notice leads with.
fields.notes: Should equal tax + penalties + interest; a mismatch means a component was missed.

fields.name: serviceCenter
fields.prompt: Extract the IRS office or service center that issued the notice, from the return address block or the payment address.
fields.notes: Determines where the response is mailed.

extraction.notes: CP14 is typically 2-3 pages with the balance breakdown on page 1. If the components do not sum to the stated total, re-read page 2 — an accrued amount is often listed separately.

validation.description: Validate that the response commits to a concrete path, does not concede an assessment the taxpayer may contest, and does not leave available penalty relief unclaimed.

rules.name: deadlineCompliance
rules.message: Respond by the pay-by date printed on the notice. Penalties and interest continue to accrue past it.
rules.example_fail: Notice due June 23; response mailed July 10.
rules.example_pass: Notice due June 23; response postmarked June 16.

rules.name: responsePathChosen
rules.check: response commits to payment, installment agreement, OIC, CNC, or a dispute
rules.message: Choose a path: pay in full, request an installment agreement, submit an offer, request hardship status, or dispute the assessment.
rules.example_fail: A letter acknowledging the balance without proposing anything.
rules.example_pass: A letter requesting a 36-month installment agreement with Form 9465 enclosed.

rules.name: penaltyReliefConsidered
rules.check: if abatable penalties assessed: relief requested or eligibility ruled out
rules.message: Penalties were assessed but no relief was requested. First Time Abate is not automatic and must be asked for.
rules.example_fail: A $210 failure-to-pay penalty is paid without asking, on an otherwise clean record.
rules.example_pass: The response requests First Time Abate, citing three prior years filed and paid on time.

rules.name: noLiabilityAdmission
rules.message: Do not admit fault. Proposing to pay is not the same as conceding the assessment is correct or that a penalty is deserved.
rules.example_fail: We apologize for our error in failing to pay on time.
rules.example_pass: We are enclosing payment for the balance shown and separately request abatement of the penalty.

rules.name: supportingDocumentation
rules.check: if_contesting or requesting relief: evidence attached
rules.message: Attach proof for whatever is claimed: payment records if the balance is already paid, or evidence of the circumstances if relief is requested on reasonable cause.
rules.example_fail: Asserting the balance was paid, with nothing enclosed.
rules.example_pass: Enclosing an EFTPS confirmation and a bank statement showing the debit.

rules.name: correctAddressing
rules.check: response addressed to the issuing center with SSN and tax year referenced
rules.message: Address the response to the issuing service center and reference your SSN and tax year so it is matched to the account.
rules.example_fail: Sent to a general IRS address with no account reference.

rules.name: professionalFormat
rules.message: Use a formal business letter with a proper address, date and signature.
rules.example_fail: A handwritten note on the notice stub.
rules.example_pass: A typed letter to the Kansas City Service Center, dated and signed.

validation.notes: The most consequential CP14 failure is doing nothing. The second is paying a penalty that would have been abated on request.

aiPrompt.system: You are a tax correspondence specialist experienced in IRS collection procedure. You write letters that commit to a specific, achievable resolution and that preserve every option the taxpayer still has. You never concede that an assessment is correct, and you never describe a penalty as deserved.
aiPrompt.task: Analyse the extracted CP14 data and the taxpayer's circumstances. Determine the appropriate path — payment in full, installment agreement, offer in compromise, currently-not-collectible status, or dispute — and draft the corresponding response. Where abatable penalties were assessed, include a penalty relief request stating the basis. Where the taxpayer asserts the balance is wrong or already paid, state that position with the enclosed proof and request that the account be corrected.
aiPrompt.format: Professional business letter addressed to the issuing IRS service center, suitable for filing.
constraints: Never admit fault, error, or that a penalty is warranted; proposing payment is not conceding the assessment
State one clear, specific path — do not present several options for the IRS to choose between
For an installment agreement, propose a concrete monthly figure and a start date
Request penalty relief separately from any payment proposal, so paying does not undercut the request
Do not claim First Time Abate eligibility unless the taxpayer confirms three clean prior years
Cite only documents the taxpayer actually has
Do not state what the law requires; state facts and enclose proof
Reference the tax year, SSN and notice date so the response is matched to the account

examples.output:
We are writing in response to your CP14 notice dated June 2, 2025 regarding tax year 2024.

We are requesting an installment agreement for the balance shown. Enclosed is Form 9465 proposing monthly payments of $200, beginning July 15, 2025, by direct debit. We understand interest continues to accrue on the unpaid balance during the agreement.

Separately, we request abatement of the $210.00 failure-to-pay penalty under the First Time Abate provisions of IRM 20.1.1.3.3.2.1. Our returns for tax years 2021, 2022 and 2023 were each filed on time and the tax shown was paid in full, and no penalties were assessed for those periods. We ask that the penalty and the interest attributable to it be removed from the account.

This request is not an acknowledgement that the penalty was correctly assessed.

aiPrompt.notes: The single highest-value thing this workflow does is surface penalty relief. Most CP14 recipients pay the penalty without knowing First Time Abate exists, and the notice does not tell them.

responseTemplate.description: Business letter responding to a CP14 balance due notice.

sections.name: header
sections.template:
[IRS Service Center Address]

RE: CP14 Notice Response
Tax Year [Tax Year]
SSN: [SSN]
Notice Date: [Notice Date]

[Taxpayer Name]
[Taxpayer Address]

[Date]
sections.guidance: Address to the issuing service center. The RE: block is how the IRS matches the letter to the account.
sections.example:
Internal Revenue Service
Kansas City, MO 64999-0052

RE: CP14 Notice Response
Tax Year 2024
SSN: 123-45-6789
Notice Date: June 2, 2025

John Michael Smith
412 Oak Street
Springfield, MO 65807

June 16, 2025

sections.name: introduction
sections.template:
Dear Sir or Madam:

We are writing in response to your CP14 notice dated [Notice Date] regarding tax year [Tax Year].
sections.guidance: One sentence identifying the notice being answered.
sections.example:
Dear Sir or Madam:

We are writing in response to your CP14 notice dated June 2, 2025 regarding tax year 2024.

sections.name: itemByItemResponse
sections.template: [Position on the balance and the chosen resolution path]
sections.guidance: State the path: payment enclosed, installment agreement with a specific monthly amount and start date, offer in compromise, hardship status, or a dispute with the basis and enclosed proof. Generated from the taxpayer's stated position.
sections.example: We are requesting an installment agreement for the balance shown. Enclosed is Form 9465 proposing monthly payments of $200, beginning July 15, 2025, by direct debit.

sections.name: penaltyRelief
sections.template: Separately, we request abatement of the penalties assessed for tax year [Tax Year]. This request is not an acknowledgement that the penalties were correctly assessed.
sections.guidance: Include whenever abatable penalties were assessed. Keep it separate from the payment proposal so that paying does not undercut the request. State the basis — First Time Abate, or specific reasonable-cause facts with evidence.
sections.example: Separately, we request abatement of the $210.00 failure-to-pay penalty under the First Time Abate provisions. Our returns for 2021, 2022 and 2023 were each filed on time and paid in full, with no penalties assessed.

sections.name: conclusion
sections.template: Please confirm receipt of this response and update the account accordingly. We can be reached at the address above.
sections.guidance: Short close requesting confirmation and account update.
sections.example: Please confirm receipt of this response and update the account accordingly.

sections.name: signature
sections.template:
Sincerely,

[Taxpayer Name]
SSN: [SSN]

Enclosures:
[List of Attached Documents]
sections.guidance: Sign and list every enclosure so the IRS can confirm nothing is missing.
sections.example:
Sincerely,

John Michael Smith
SSN: 123-45-6789

Enclosures:
- Form 9465 Installment Agreement Request

legalFramework.description: CP14 is the notice and demand for payment required by IRC 6303 after an assessment. It starts the collection notice sequence and the running of the failure-to-pay penalty at the higher rate once a levy notice issues.
authorities: IRC 6303 — Notice and demand for tax, required within 60 days of assessment
IRC 6601 — Interest on underpayment, compounded daily
IRC 6651(a)(2) — Failure-to-pay penalty, 0.5% per month up to 25%
IRC 6651(a)(1) — Failure-to-file penalty, 5% per month up to 25%
IRM 20.1.1.3.3.2.1 — First Time Abate administrative penalty relief
precedents: CP14 does not itself authorise levy; it begins the notice sequence that leads to CP501, CP503, CP504 and finally CP90
Requesting an installment agreement suspends levy action while the request is pending
First Time Abate is administrative relief granted on request, not automatically applied
Proposing or making payment does not waive the right to contest the underlying assessment or to seek a refund
Interest on the tax continues to accrue during an installment agreement
criticalRules: Do not ignore this notice. Doing nothing is the most common and most costly response — the balance advances automatically toward levy.
The pay-by date printed on the notice controls. Do not compute a substitute date.
Request penalty relief explicitly. First Time Abate is never applied on its own and the notice does not mention it exists.
Keep the penalty relief request separate from the payment proposal, so that paying does not read as agreement that the penalty was owed.
Never state or imply that the taxpayer was at fault, even while proposing to pay.
Do not claim First Time Abate without confirming the three prior years were filed and paid on time; a false claim is refused and wastes the window.
If the balance was already paid, say so and enclose the proof rather than paying twice.

jurisdictionVariations.variation: CP14 procedures are uniform nationwide under the Internal Revenue Code.

Taxpayers in a federally declared disaster area may have deadlines postponed under IRC 7508A. Check current IRS disaster relief announcements for the taxpayer's county before treating a deadline as missed.

testCases.description: Cover the ordinary installment path, the penalty-relief opportunity, and the case where the balance is already paid.

cases.name: cp14-installment-with-abatement
cases.description: Standard balance due with a failure-to-pay penalty and a clean prior record
cases.inputDocument: CP14 showing tax $4,200.00, failure-to-pay penalty $210.00, interest $63.40, total $4,473.40 for tax year 2024
cases.expectedResponse: Letter requesting an installment agreement with a specific monthly amount, plus a separate First Time Abate request citing three clean prior years.
successCriteria: Components sum to the stated total
A concrete monthly payment and start date are proposed
Penalty relief is requested separately from the payment proposal
No admission of fault anywhere in the letter

cases.name: cp14-already-paid
cases.description: The taxpayer paid before the notice was generated; the payment crossed in the mail
cases.inputDocument: CP14 for tax year 2024 total $2,150.00, where the taxpayer holds an EFTPS confirmation dated before the notice date
cases.expectedResponse: Letter stating the balance was paid on the confirmed date, enclosing the EFTPS confirmation and bank statement, and requesting the account be corrected and any penalty and interest removed.
successCriteria: Payment proof is enclosed and listed
The letter does not propose paying again
Removal of penalty and interest attributable to the crossed payment is requested
No admission that the balance was owed

cases.name: cp14-estimated-tax-penalty
cases.description: Edge case: the only penalty assessed is the estimated tax penalty, which First Time Abate does not cover
cases.inputDocument: CP14 with an estimated tax penalty of $340.00 and no failure-to-file or failure-to-pay penalty
cases.expectedResponse: Letter proposing payment without a First Time Abate request, since the estimated tax penalty is outside FTA and has its own narrow exceptions.
successCriteria: No First Time Abate request is generated
The penalty relief rule does not fire on a non-abatable penalty
Any relief sought is framed under the estimated tax penalty exceptions instead

relatedWorkflows.description: CP14 sits at the head of the collection notice sequence.
upstream: cp2000 — an underreporter adjustment that was assessed produces the balance a CP14 demands
cp3219a — an uncontested deficiency becomes an assessment and then a CP14
downstream: cp501 — first reminder when a CP14 goes unanswered
cp504 — notice of intent to levy on state tax refunds
cp90 — final notice of intent to levy with Collection Due Process rights
cp523 — installment agreement default, if an agreement is later missed
alternatives: form-656 — offer in compromise where the balance cannot be paid in full
form-433-a — collection information statement supporting hardship or an offer

implementation.notes: Highest-volume IRS notice by a wide margin. The workflow's distinctive value is surfacing First Time Abate, which most recipients never learn about.
knownChallenges: Separating tax from penalty from interest when the notice presents a single total on page 1
Establishing First Time Abate eligibility, which depends on three prior years the notice says nothing about
Not generating a First Time Abate request for the estimated tax penalty, which it does not cover
Handling crossed payments, where the balance was paid before the notice was generated
